canonical_statement: The study compared thrombotic and bleeding outcomes between low-intensity and standard-intensity therapeutic intravenous UFH protocols.
The retrospective cohort included 377 adults who received therapeutic UFH from July 2011 through July 2017 at a single tertiary academic center.

population.label: Adults receiving therapeutic intravenous unfractionated heparin at a single tertiary academic center, July 2011-July 2017

canonical_statement: Patients on a separate acute coronary syndrome UFH protocol and patients receiving concomitant thrombolytic agents were excluded; only LI or SI protocol patients were analyzed.

population.label: Therapeutic UFH recipients eligible for LI or SI protocol comparison
inclusion_criteria: Received LI or SI therapeutic UFH protocol
exclusion_criteria: Separate acute coronary syndrome UFH protocol

canonical_statement: Protocol assignment to low intensity or standard intensity was determined by the ordering physician based on clinical judgment of bleeding risk, thrombotic risk, and treatment indication.
Anti-Xa activity was used preferentially over aPTT to monitor in-vivo UFH activity.
The low-intensity protocol used an optional 60 units/kg bolus and an initial infusion rate of 12 units/kg/hr.

exposures.details: Target anti-Xa 0.25-0.35 IU/mL; initial infusion 12 units/kg/hr; optional 60 units/kg bolus.

canonical_statement: The standard-intensity protocol used a suggested 80 units/kg bolus and an initial infusion rate of 18 units/kg/hr.

exposures.details: Target anti-Xa 0.30-0.70 IU/mL; initial infusion 18 units/kg/hr; suggested 80 units/kg bolus.

canonical_statement: The LI titration algorithm specified: anti-Xa <0.11, bolus 60 units/kg and increase 3 units/kg/hr; 0.11-0.24, bolus 30 units/kg and increase 2 units/kg/hr; 0.25-0.35, no change; 0.36-0.55, decrease 2 units/kg/hr; >0.56, hold 60 minutes and decrease 3 units/kg/hr.

exposures.details: Target anti-Xa 0.25-0.35 IU/mL; initial infusion 12 units/kg/hr; optional 60 units/kg bolus.

canonical_statement: The SI titration algorithm specified: anti-Xa <0.2, bolus 80 units/kg and increase 4 units/kg/hr; 0.2-0.29, bolus 40 units/kg and increase 2 units/kg/hr; 0.30-0.70, no change; 0.71-0.80, decrease 1 unit/kg/hr; 0.81-0.90, hold 30 minutes and decrease 2 units/kg/hr; >0.91, hold 60 minutes and decrease 3 units/kg/hr.

exposures.details: Target anti-Xa 0.30-0.70 IU/mL; initial infusion 18 units/kg/hr; suggested 80 units/kg bolus.

canonical_statement: UFH dose calculations used total body weight at 125 kg or less and adjusted body weight above 125 kg.
Anti-Xa levels were obtained six hours after infusion initiation and every six hours until two consecutive therapeutic measurements, then every morning.
The primary outcomes were new or worsening thrombus and bleeding occurring while patients received intravenous UFH.

concept.text: New or worsening thrombus and bleeding while on UFH

canonical_statement: Bleeding was categorized as major or minor using ISTH definitions; major bleeding included fatal bleeding, critical-organ bleeding, a hemoglobin decline greater than 2 g/dL, or red-cell transfusion.

outcome.definition: Fatal bleeding, critical-organ bleeding, >2 g/dL hemoglobin decline, or red blood cell transfusion.

canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes included transfusion requirement within one month and death within three months of UFH initiation.

The investigators performed manual EMR chart review with REDCap data capture and used descriptive statistics, Fisher exact testing, t tests or Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, then stepwise multivariable logistic regression for variables significant in univariate analysis.
The study was approved by the University of Florida IRB under project IRB201702116.
Of 377 patients, 158 (42.0%) received the LI protocol and 219 (58.0%) received the SI protocol.

canonical_statement: The authors observed that similar HAS-BLED distributions did not distinguish the clinically higher-risk LI group from the SI group.
The authors concluded that HAS-BLED did not appear applicable for determining bleeding risk in patients receiving UFH and that a UFH-specific risk score remained needed.
The study was retrospective and nonrandomized.
The LI group was selected because clinicians considered patients at higher bleeding risk, creating substantial baseline imbalance and confounding by indication.
The authors concluded that the LI protocol may have comparable efficacy to SI based on similar observed incidence of new or worsening thrombus.
The abstract states that an anti-Xa target of 0.25-0.35 IU/mL may be more optimal for high-risk patients.

The authors called for a prospective randomized comparison matched for comorbidities, risk factors, and indications to clarify the findings and support risk-stratification and dosing-nomogram development.
